srd.intent: Digital reference; unchanged in this print revision

production.light: RGB digital-print interior; no bleed required

artPlacements.role: Show companions making different useful contributions at the same table. The illustration supports the choices in the prose; it is not a set of prescribed classes.
Place the transparent rope, hook, flask, map, and lantern beside the task sequence. Each object is explicitly used by the example, so the spot art functions as an equipment inventory.
The porter’s preserved delivery evokes duty carried across generations. Use it beside the example of inherited work and chosen obligation, without implying that undead appearance grants mechanics.
Use the rescue scene to annotate visible resources, intended outcome, and two alternative routes. The image makes the players’ questions concrete rather than decorating a generic introduction.
The guardian at a narrow entrance provides a concrete distinction between ordinary passage, a granted exceptional method, and a permission that still has boundaries.
Use the makers’ table as a construction metaphor, then pair it with ingredient labels supplied by the layout. The picture supports assembly; the text explains reference identity.
Arrange the pictured tools beside a ledger-and-reference diagram. Each object is counted once while appearing in several uses, making the ownership distinction tangible.

The maintenance unit and its work-order dispute anchor the distinction between noticing, reasoning, recalling, and persuading. Its appearance is evidence in the scene, not an automatic combat challenge.

The civic witness protects testimony. Place its figure beside the comparison of a witnessed event, a recorded statement, and an interpretation; the portrait supplies no automatic truth-detection power.
The rooted listener illustrates a location learned through contact rather than sight. Mark the contacted surface in the composition, making the sense’s actual medium and limits visible.
The lynx’s low posture and ruined-observatory setting support a scene about tracks, concealment, and changing lines of sight. The image must not imply an unlisted invisibility power.
Use the surveyor’s beam geometry beside a plan of intervening surfaces. The illustration grounds delivery and obstacles without granting its abilities to the reader’s character.
The bridge rescue provides several recipients within one threatened space. Annotate people, structures, and water separately to show why choosing an area does not supply automatic selectivity.

The tools support two contrasting rescue methods with different practical burdens. Place the rope beside the ordinary route and the flask beside the extraordinary route, rather than illustrating Cost as damage alone.

A camp under temporary protection makes continuation meaningful: someone keeps watch, a working supports shelter, and the others need rest. Use the scene to contrast active maintenance with a completed physical task.
The loading machine supports failing freight above workers. Show its load and the party’s different positions so cooperation reads as divided tasks, not a repeated bonus icon.
The rooftop challenger anchors a round about positioning, a contested banner, and a route to safety. The art should show ledges and a shared objective rather than present a static combat portrait.
The flying rescuer supports an example of responding to a perceived fall. Compose it near the ledge and rope so the reader sees the opportunity and the limits of reach.
Return to the bridge from a lower viewpoint, emphasizing a caught rope and newly exposed route. The changed composition should make the useful aftermath of failure visible.

The herd at the ford illustrates space, young animals, and a retreat route. Use a wider scene or annotated crop to teach passage and observation rather than presenting a creature as a compulsory enemy.

The monument attendant and a marked stone support a scene about repairs, visitors, and trace evidence. Compose the portrait beside a sequence of three material clues; the art must not imply universal access to the past.
The disputed-contract spirit illustrates words with consequences. Put the document and opposing parties in the composition, making terms and obligations the subject of the spread.

The urgent workshop courier supports route choices, information carried between settlements, and the need to protect a delivery. Place it with a map and visible cargo rather than a generic wilderness backdrop.

The caravan repairer supports a task with spare parts, tools, carried supplies, and equipment actively in use. Show hands and objects clearly; do not turn the art into a list of free mechanical benefits.

The camp should show the conditions of rest: shelter, watch, bedding, and companions helping one another. Pair it with an actual-used recovery ledger, rather than portraying elapsed time as automatic healing.

The restoration guardian illustrates protection of an injured explorer. Compose the explorer, immediate hazard, and assisting companions so the reader sees distinct rescue tasks rather than a generic healer portrait.

The makers’ workshop becomes a scene of reflection and altered plans. Show a familiar working being revised, supporting continuity of concept rather than depicting advancement as an unrelated arsenal.

Use the transparent map, lantern, and writing objects as a small margin composition beside a paper-record example. The image reinforces practical offline play and must not become another required digital tool.

Show the Candlebone Porter carrying its protected delivery; the parcel, destination and blocked route must remain visible. Its undead silhouette establishes a possible threat while the surrounding scene communicates a task that can be completed peacefully.

Place the Mossback Grazer between the ford and its young, with the caravan’s stranded cart visible on the facing page. The picture should explain its defensive motive and why a different route changes the encounter.

Show the Hollowbark Listener touching rooted stone beside a shrine; distinguish the connected ground from a hanging walkway. Use the picture to support the question of where its published contact-based sense applies, without treating decorative rings as a new radius.

Show the Moonspoor Lynx partly concealed among the observatory’s broken lenses. Include readable disturbed dust and an empty nearby alcove so the image separates evidence of presence from certain target location.

Place the Rainspout Artillerist on its drainage tower, with a wall, broken railing and exposed courtyard shown from one clear viewpoint. Overlay only labels for the actual projected paths discussed in the text; the illustration must teach why two routes have different cover.

Show the Counterlift Atlas supporting a tilted freight platform while a trapped worker and reachable anchor point remain visible. The composition should let the reader trace a rescue dependency from support to tether to evacuation, rather than depict an unrelated fight.

Show the Skyhook Corsair approaching an airship by its carried hook, with landing rail and retreat route clearly separated. The facing sketch can label the player’s 10-ft and 20-ft movements; the portrait does not substitute for either actor’s actual movement record.

Show the Wingstitch Chirurgeon close enough to catch one falling companion while a second person stands farther along the damaged span. This relationship makes eligible immediate scope visible; avoid depicting universal rescue of every airborne creature.

Place the Sinkhole Maw below a cracked hunting floor, with three visibly different exits around its breach. The artwork should telegraph disturbance and likely approach; mark any actual trap boundary only from its saved definition, not from dramatic cracks.

Show the Briar Covenant Tender attending an injured grove defender, with the threatened sapling between them and approaching visitors. The illustration explains a support relationship and a protection objective rather than treating the Tender as a generic magical healer.

Show the Cloudglass Harrier aligned with a clear gap between drifting ruin towers. The gap, shelter and moving platform should matter as much as the creature, making a beam’s usable lane and an alternate crossing visible.

Use the Walking Foundry at a scale that shows nearby occupied streets and a fuel route. Its body should dominate the spread while clear evacuation paths and the fuel destination remain visible, supporting a solo objective beyond reducing its Vitality.

Show the Airshare Nautilus beside a flooded stair and a conscious stranded person, with the breathing apparatus prominent. Use the facing situation diagram to distinguish reaching the person, sharing breath and reaching shelter; do not imply the creature restores Vitality by proximity.

Show the Bellwatch Hound following a worn coat through a crowded lane, with its handler visibly studying the same trail. The illustration should emphasize a physical scent source and the possibility of a transferred object, rather than supernatural detection of guilt.

Show the Null Choir Node’s chamber with a visible performer maintaining a separate light source near an exit. Light, source and shelter should be visually distinguishable; the image illustrates competing continuing work, not an invented universal cancellation aura.

Show the Mnemonic Surgeon addressing one distressed subject across an ordinary workbench, with its tools set aside. The composition should make a bounded support exchange clear and avoid implying that the creature reads or rewrites every mind nearby.

Show the Silkgear Patchwright repairing a caravan seam, with one identifiable tool and one repeated stitch motif. Beside it, the design can trace a single acquired ingredient into several organizations; the illustration’s repeated marks must not look like multiple bought copies.

Use the Saltwound Leviathan’s wounded silhouette beside small shipping craft, with a clear alternate channel. The scale conveys danger, while wound and route explain why treatment or diversion can matter. Do not add anatomical attack labels that the saved build does not contain.

The Stillpoint Orb’s nested rings and suspended fragments make the actual containment subject legible. Relate that portrait to a small plan showing the prepared boundary, its source and an accessible observation point; readers should see why inspecting the edge changes a decision.

The Waxseal Witness’s civic form belongs beside a hearing involving protected testimony. Its wax tools and careful posture should introduce the difference between preserving a statement and deciding whether that statement proves a wider claim.

Use the Velvet Oath Broker’s contract-bearing silhouette to frame a bounded negotiation. Place the entry being offered and the promise being requested together in the spread’s composition, so the reader connects elegance and temptation to actual terms rather than assumed supernatural compulsion.

The Stone Script Reader’s mosaic hands, worn slab and repair wheel explain evidence with physical provenance. Use the portrait beside a simple relationship of observation, maintenance record and authored recollection; the art supports material memory without implying omniscience.

The Thornpath Jackal’s wiry body and root-crossing pose should introduce a pack following a caravan through broken ground. Relate its portrait to food, roots and exposed travelers as actual subjects; do not use it as an unrelated wilderness ornament.

The Rootbound Aegis’s shield, roots and sanctuary threshold establish protection as a task performed in a particular place. Place its portrait near the shelter’s entrance plan and rest record, connecting the guardian’s role to what permits recovery rather than implying automatic healing.

The Ledger-Eater Imp and its stolen records are the visual center of a practical preparation workshop. Use the contract, hiding place and repair need as related subjects around the portrait, demonstrating that a creature’s nuisance can connect people and routes without copying a predetermined adventure sequence.

The Ashwake Mourner’s attentive, protective figure should anchor an aftermath rather than a generic undead battle. Pair it with survivors, a recovered token or a quiet refuge only as the worked situation requires; the image’s purpose is to make care and a changed relationship visible.
